newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Cano Limon oil field still shut down.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Cano Limon oil field still shut down.

text.p: Colombia's Cano Limon oil field remained shut down Monday, four days after leftist rebels dynamited the massive pipeline linking it to the Caribbean port of Covenas, a spokesman for Occidental Petroleum Corp said.
Robert Stewart, manager of corporate affairs at Occidental's office in Bogota, said repairs to the pipeline had been made impossible by the "public order situation in the area."

He did not elaborate, but 10 soldiers were killed by guerrillas when they attempted to secure the region in northeast Arauca province where the pipeline was crippled Thursday and troops have apparently been unable to move back into the area.

Stewart said the pipeline attack, the 37th this year, had already forced the state oil company Ecopetrol to declare force majeure in the Covena oil terminal, thereby cutting standby payments to oil tankers by 50 percent.

Ecopetrol officials could not be reached for immediate comment, but industry sources said Occidential and Ecopetrol were now considering the possibility of declaring force majeure on the Cano Limon field as well.
"We're in a supremely diffficult situation," Stewart said. He declined, however, to comment on the possible force majeure declaration.

The Cano Limon field normally produces 180,000 barrels of crude oil per day but Stewart said production had recently been scaled back to 171,000 bpd because of law-and-order problems in and around the field.
